summary: Allen Wright Thrasher is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1974) and learned from traditional teachers Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He held a post at the Library of Congress (~1987–2013).
Indologist Allison Busch studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held a position as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Würzburg (PhD 1874–1879) and under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, the State Museum, Lucknow, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Alois Müller worked in religious studies and linguistics. He held posts at Vienna University Library (~1868–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and served as Direktor at Graz University Library (1879).

Aloysius Pieris specialized in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sacred Heart College, University of London, Pontifical Theological Faculty of Southern Italy, University of Sri Lanka, Tilburg University, and under Bernard de Give. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1980–1986) under supervisor Yasuaki Nara.

Alvappillai Veluppillai was an Indology, religious studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon under K. Kanapathypillai and Oxford under Thomas Burrow. He held positions at Ceylon, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

Amalananda Ghosh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1936–1937), he served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and as a fellow at IIAS (1968–1971).
Amalia Pezzali works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied under T. R. V. Murti as a doctoral student and under Michel Hulin.

Amanda Goodman works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under A. K. Warder (attested 1984) and was taught by Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, M. Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali works in linguistics and Indology. She has held posts as Lecturer in Urdu at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2026) and at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948), and Vice-President of the Ganganatha Jha Research Institute.

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1953–1959). He held positions at Jadavpur, Delhi, the London School of Economics (~1971–1977), and Harvard University (~2004).
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Hyderabad in 2009 and serves there as Professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied under Mary Margaret McCabe, Verity Harte, Raimond Gaita, Jonathan Lear, Susan Neiman, and Jonathan Glover, and has held positions including Associate Professor at Yale-NUS College.
Amdo Zen Karwa Chökyi Sengé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Amelia Bonea is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2006) and Heidelberg University (~2006–2012), and became Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (~2020).

Amelia Hall specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford (2012) and held faculty positions at Naropa University and Central Michigan University (attested 2019).
